claim: One-shot training with immediate feedback and practice (game) cuts bias by roughly 32-46% at once in people and about 24-35% two to three months later; a passive video also helps (19-26%) but less in Exp 1.
agent_test: Add a per-bias practice-with-feedback block vs a warning block at equal tokens; measure bias score at once and on a held-out set later.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Game beats video clearly only for some biases (blind spot, FAE, confirmation, projection); for anchoring and representativeness video equals game. Gain from feedback is bias-specific. Game and video also differ in practice, coaching and interactivity, so feedback is not isolated (gap 3).
agent_test: Compare feedback vs no-feedback prompts per bias family.

claim: Knowing about biases is not the same as being debiased: video raised bias knowledge more but did not debias more; knowledge fell to near equal by follow-up.
agent_test: Compare 'name the bias' warning vs procedure/feedback at equal tokens.

claim: Debiasing generalised to untrained facets of the same bias (confirmation facets d=.79 post, .65 follow-up) and to unseen problem formats.
agent_test: Train on 3 task variants, test on 3 untaught variants.

claim: Human training transfers to the field at a smaller size: trained MBA students were about 19% (corrected from 29%) less likely to pick the confirming option in an unannounced Challenger-style case; no decay over 43-52 days; mechanism was fewer confirming arguments. Gap search: the published abstract and PubMed give 19% and list a 2020 Corrigendum; the accepted manuscript still said 29%, so the correction is almost certainly 29% to 19% (corrigendum text not read). Assignment was by class schedule, not random.
agent_test: Embed an unannounced confirmation trap inside a long task; compare disconfirm-first operator vs none.

claim: Analysts study: one-shot training lowered confirmation bias from pretest to posttest in national risk analysts and students (general-domain partial eta2 .384, risk-domain .215), but there was no untrained control group and two authors are the original game team, so this is not an independent replication.
agent_test: Run the analyst-style case on the agent with and without the training block.

claim: Short forecasting training (under 1 hour; CHAMPS KNOW) improved Brier score 6-11% over control across four tournament years (abstract re-checked); part of the gain via practice.
agent_test: Test probability-reasoning module on forecasting questions at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Rule training generalises to everyday reasoning: brief training in cost-benefit / statistical rules raised normative answers (44% vs 28.6% in Larrick 1990 Study 2); Nisbett 1987 abstract confirms brief rule training can transfer. Original Nisbett numbers not read.
agent_test: Give explicit rule cards (sunk cost, base rate) vs none.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Training transfer is limited by bias type: analogical training improved only statistical-principle biases (N=154, 4 weeks); awareness training alone did not help others; a one-shot workshop cut but did not remove anchoring in developers (d 1.19 to 0.72).
agent_test: Test per-bias, do not claim general debiasing.

claim: Cognitive forcing / checklists often fail: tool null in 76 doctors (2.8 vs 3.1 correct); delaying or slowing did not stop people following biased AI advice (n=281, 373).
schema_part: G (do not rely on generic slow-down)
agent_test: Compare forced-pause prompt vs targeted procedure.

claim: In LLMs, a loop that detects the bias, analyses it and rewrites the prompt (SACD) gives the lowest bias: Llama-3.1-8B FOMC 0.3805 to 0.157; GPT-4o 0.365 to 0.030 (re-checked in paper tables). Self-help rewrite is the strongest simple baseline. One research group only. Gap search: ablation shows both the detect step and the analysis step matter (w/o all = self-help: FOMC 0.3490 vs 0.1175), but compute is not matched and gpt-4o was the strongest model tested.
agent_test: Replicate SACD vs one-pass self-help at equal tokens; SACD costs extra calls so match budgets.

claim: Generic LLM prompting is weak against biases: CoT, Reflexion, multi-agent debate, few-shot give little or worse; Reflexion and debate can amplify bias with multiple biases; few-shot debias can cause refusal or accept-all.
schema_part: G (no debate by default), 4b not to add
agent_test: Benchmark debate/reflexion vs single-agent rewrite under token parity.

claim: Awareness prompt effects in LLMs are model-dependent: helps weaker models (GPT-3.5) on some biases, little on GPT-4; can backfire; self-help needs strong models (weak models change 40-52% of decisions).
agent_test: Test awareness prompt across model sizes.

claim: Prompt-level debiasing is family-dependent: +40.5% on response-position bias but -4.4% accuracy on judgment bias; superficial debiasing flags over 90% of unbiased content as biased (Llama2-7B).
agent_test: Always measure false-alarm rate on unbiased items.

claim: Anchoring in LLMs is shallow and not removed by CoT, ignore-the-anchor or reflection; a set-standard-first two-phase prompt gives about 10 points (34.7% to 24.7% on Llama-3.1-8B); reasoning models lowest.
agent_test: Anchor-resistant estimate protocol vs CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Consider-the-alternative style prompts help LLMs that reason long: Dual-Goal / Think-in-Opposites raised Wason rule discovery from 42% to 56% on average across 11 LLMs (Jhaveri et al. 2026, arXiv 2604.02485, identity now confirmed); gains were significant only for thinking models. Human basis: Hirt and Markman 1995 and Branchini 2023.
agent_test: Run 2-4-6 style tasks with and without opposite-test operator.

claim: Training LLMs (not prompting) so a bias cue is non-predictive generalises: Qwen3-4B adversarial accuracy 70.1 to 83.3, unseen-distraction robustness +39.1. Outside our no-training scope; supports practice with feedback as an analogue only.
agent_test: Not testable without training; design hint: present bias cues as uninformative.

claim: Human-style intervention packages translated to LLMs (DIY: stereotype replacement, perspective-taking, etc.) cut mean bias to 2% at 90% reasoning accuracy and transfer up to 14.8 pp to unseen dimensions.
agent_test: Replicate REVISE-only variant at equal tokens.

claim: Instruction tuning / RLHF can add decoy, certainty and belief biases; LLMs show human-like biases across 30 types; small vignette changes break GPT-3.
agent_test: Baseline bias audit before adding a scaffold.

claim: No LLM study replicates the human game design (feedback on own errors over repeated rounds, delayed retest); closest are SACD loops and RL training.
agent_test: Test an in-run error log with immediate feedback vs none on repeated item sets.

claim: Skeptical position (Arkes 1991; Milkman 2009; Kahneman): training works only when reminders exist; field transfer and Hawthorne effects are open. Partly answered by Sellier 2019 and the analyst study but no large independent replication.
agent_test: Test transfer with no cue present.

claim: Listing many counterfactual alternatives can backfire in people: 10 alternatives raised hindsight bias, 2 alternatives did not (Sanna, Schwarz, Stocker 2002; brow-contraction replication 2003). No LLM test of the number of alternatives exists in what was found.
agent_test: Run the agent with 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 alternatives on hindsight and confirmation items; plot bias against list length.

claim: The human game-over-video gain is confounded: games added practice, coaching and interactivity along with feedback. Game variants (scores, hints, narrative, first round only) did not differ, so one round of practice plus an after-action review may carry most of the effect. No ablation isolates the active ingredient.
agent_test: Ablate: warning only, warning plus worked example, practice without feedback, practice with feedback, one round vs three; equal tokens.

claim: Prompt debiasing is judged by bias score but can hide avoidance: models flag bias in clean text, answer 'Unknown', and lose accuracy; SACD adds a small false-alarm rate (3-12 of 500) and a larger wrong-bias-type rate (49-108 of 500). Always report accuracy and false alarms on clean items.
agent_test: Add clean (unbiased) twins to every bias test item; report accuracy, refusal rate and false-flag rate with each debiasing step.

claim: Cue-ignoring learned on one content cue (bandwagon) transfers to other content cues (authority, distraction) but not to a structural cue (answer position) in weight-trained Qwen3-4B; wrong-only training teaches a shortcut that hurts when the cue is right. Transfer in judgment-bias families under in-context training is untested.
agent_test: Include cases where the cue is correct; test transfer between bias families with in-context practice only.

claim: Independent replication of the Morewedge/Sellier training results has not been found. All field and expert studies (Sellier 2019 quasi-experiment, analysts 2025 pre-post) share authors with the original game; the analysts study has no untrained control.
agent_test: Treat the human effect as promising, one research group; do not set the agent's expected effect from it.

claim: Decay of debiasing over steps in an agent run has no direct study. Human retention was 2-3 months at about 24-35% (game) and no decay across 11 vs 43-52 days in the field; LLM side only shows that an AI-labelled prior can raise anchoring by 52% in recent commercial models.
agent_test: Insert the debiasing block at step 1 vs every k steps; measure bias on probe items placed at steps 5, 20, 50.
